frontier.hypothesis: The flag section's SHAPE — a loop over a bit index rather than three unrolled blocks — has never been varied, and the s6 RTL model makes it materially more interesting than it looked to s5: since the address form of an access is fixed one-to-one by its C spelling at expansion, a loop body contains exactly ONE flag-byte read and ONE flag-byte store, so the store-to-load forward question is asked once per iteration across a loop back-edge instead of three times in straight-line code.
frontier.mechanism: cse's value table is invalidated across a loop back-edge (cse_end_of_basic_block terminates the block at the loop's CODE_LABEL when the label has more than one use), so a loop-carried read of the flag byte cannot be forwarded from the previous iteration's store. If GCC then peels or unrolls, the peeled form is a genuinely new chassis whose reads were born un-forwardable; if it emits a real loop, the shape is refuted immediately by the objdump. Either outcome is decisive and neither has ever been measured.
frontier.next_probe: Write the flag section as `for (k = 1; k <= 4; k <<= 1) { c = p[8] & k; val = *ptr; val2 = val | k; if (!c) val2 = val; *ptr = val2; }` and as an explicit three-iteration variant over a local index, score both with `sandbox func_80034F88 --disable all`, and read BOTH the objdump and the .cse slice (s6/forensic.py already prints the .greg header and the flag block; add the cse.fn read). rederive/synthesis modality.

frontier.hypothesis: Target's four flag-byte accesses are ALL pointer-spelled (`0(reg)`), so the original source addressed the byte through a pointer everywhere; the open question is what kept cse's canon_reg from merging the three distinct base pseudos into one address rtx — because merging them is exactly what makes the store forward into the next block's read.
frontier.mechanism: canon_reg (cse.c) rewrites a register in an address to the oldest register in its equivalence class, so two locals both initialised `= &D_80106A73;` hash identically and the forward fires (s2/s3 measured that family at 22). The forms that have NEVER been measured are the ones where the second and third bases are derived from something whose equivalence class cse cannot collapse to the first: `ptr2 = ptr;` copy chains, a base re-derived per block from a value the compiler cannot constant-fold, or a base whose class is broken by an intervening clobber. s6 established that the address rtx identity test is the WHOLE mechanism, so this is now a precisely-posed question rather than a spelling sweep.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/cse.c canon_reg + insert_regs to enumerate exactly what puts two pseudos in one qty class and what breaks a class; then build the small set of C forms that the reading says would NOT merge (copy-chained pointers, per-block re-derivation, pointer arithmetic that folds back to the same address), score each with the honest sandbox, and dump .cse for any that changes the reload count. forensics or structural modality.

frontier.hypothesis: s3's F3 escalation packet still stands and must still NOT be filed from a non-escalation modality, but s6 materially strengthens it: the packet's central claim is no longer 'cse.c:7329 blocks the reloads' (which s6 refuted) but the sharper 'the target needs four pointer-spelled accesses that do not merge, and merging is decided by canon_reg on address-rtx identity'.
frontier.mechanism: If the frontier item above comes back negative — i.e. no C form keeps two same-valued address pseudos in distinct qty classes — then honest non-volatile pure C provably cannot produce target's four 0(reg) reloads, and the two spellings that could are ruled a cheat (s2-F1, volatile pointer local) and ruled out by the volatile carve-out's two-prong gate (s3-H1). s4 adds the random-permuter negative, s5 the exhaustive directed-permuter negative, s6 the RTL-level statement of the contradiction.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT file. Two sanctioned axes remain untried (the loop-shape rederive; the canon_reg class-breaking family), and s6 alone corrected two mechanisms that three prior sessions had reasoned from while believing the family was understood. If the driver later assigns escalation modality, the packet is hypotheses.md F3 plus the s6 corrections plus the rejected/*.c headers.
